system.name: REAL
system.one_liner: a network emulator that runs unmodified containerized routers and controls their execution to converge control-plane behavior at simulator-like cost

components.name: R1
components.role: a neighbor router sending messages to R2

components.name: R3
components.role: another neighbor router sending messages to R2

components.name: R2
components.role: the router being snapshotted, taken offline, and restored

components.name: Shim
components.role: intercepts each neighbor's write() calls and R2's recv()/ppoll() calls without modifying router images

components.name: Simulated Data Plane
components.role: records, buffers and replays route messages sent to R2 to preserve its observable state across snapshot/restore

components.name: Message Log
components.role: ordered log of every route message sent to R2 while R2 is online (e.g. L=6, L=5, ..., L=1)

components.name: Buffered Messages
components.role: messages accumulated while R2 is offline, to be delivered once R2 restarts (e.g. B=4, B=3, ..., B=1)

components.name: recv()
components.role: intercepted receive call used by SimDP or R2's shim to accept incoming messages

components.name: write()
components.role: intercepted write call used by neighbors, or by SimDP during replay, to send a message

components.name: ppoll()
components.role: intercepted poll call that filters out unordered POLLIN events during replay so R2's internal events happen in the exact original order

flows.what: (a) R1's write() is intercepted and received by SimDP via recv()
(a) message appended to the ordered message log while R2 is online
(a) message popped from the log and relayed via write()/recv() to R2
(b) neighbors keep sending and SimDP keeps accepting messages even while R2 is offline
(b) messages are appended to a buffer instead of delivered, so neighbors do not detect R2 is offline
(c) recorded messages are popped and flushed from the message log for replay
(c) SimDP replays each recorded message via write()
(c) ppoll() filters out unordered POLLIN events so recv() delivers replayed messages to R2 in original order
(c) R2's own messages produced during replay are dropped rather than forwarded to neighbors

content.key_idea: SimDP preserves a router's state across a stop/restart cycle: it records every received message in order, buffers new arrivals while offline, then replays the recorded log to the restarted router in original order, dropping replay-time messages.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom through three labeled sub-figures (a), (b), (c), each read left to right through its own circled steps: recording while online, buffering while offline, then replaying to restore.

summary: REAL restarts routers instead of using costly disk-based snapshots, but must hide this from neighbors and restore exact state. Figure 7 shows how its Simulated Data Plane (SimDP) achieves this in three stacked scenarios. (a) While R2 is online, SimDP intercepts R1 and R3's writes via a Shim, receives them itself, and appends every message to an ordered Message Log before relaying it on to R2. (b) When R2 goes offline, SimDP keeps neighbors' connections alive and keeps accepting their messages, but appends them to a separate Buffered Messages queue instead of delivering them, so neighbors never detect R2 is down. (c) To restore R2, SimDP pops and replays the recorded Message Log to R2 in original order, while the Shim's intercepted ppoll() filters out unordered POLLIN events and drops any messages R2 emits during replay, so R2's internal state converges to exactly where it was before going offline.
summary_zh: 该图分三部分展示REAL的模拟数据平面如何记录回放消息以恢复路由器：(a)在线时按序记入消息日志再转发；(b)离线时消息计入缓冲队列而不投递；(c)恢复时按原顺序回放日志，过滤乱序事件。
